segments.text: Neptune is the only planet found with math. In eighteen forty-six, astronomers predicted where it should be, and found it almost exactly there.
segments.headline: Found with math

segments.text: Its winds are the fastest in the solar system, up to two thousand kilometers per hour.
One year on Neptune lasts a hundred and sixty-five Earth years. It finished its first full orbit since discovery only in twenty eleven.
Out here, sunlight is about nine hundred times dimmer than on Earth.
segments.headline: 900× dimmer sunlight

segments.text: Its largest moon, Triton, orbits backwards and shoots geysers of nitrogen into space. It may be a captured world from beyond Neptune.
segments.headline: A moon that orbits backwards

segments.text: Tomorrow, we reach a small world with a big heart. Next stop: Pluto. Follow, so you don't miss episode eight.
